audits.label: The fifteen-PR chain
audits.summary: Checked all fifteen PRs (#69–#80, #82–#84) via gh and the local clone. Every PR is OPEN with mergedAt null, and each PR's base is exactly the previous PR's head, so the chain is one straight line from main: main → m8/local-reviews-design → m8.1/contract-and-mock → m8.6/app-creation-flow → m8.7/app-local-chrome → m8.2/store-v4 → m8.3/local-snapshot-builder → m8.4/local-write-sink → m8.5/daemon-wiring → prefs/lost-update → m8.8/resync-and-pinning → m8.10/retention-and-gc → m8.11/conformance-e2e-docs → m8.9/archive-on-pr → m8.12/delete-confirm → board/m8.9-scratch-proof. No branch is behind its base (git rev-list --count head..base is 0 for all 15 adjacent pairs), every local tip equals its origin tip and GitHub's headRefOid, main == origin/main == remote main at 177068a, and merge-base(main, tip) is 177068a, so nothing needs rebasing. CI is green on every PR and is not stale: each `check` workflow run (check + conformance-matrix + e2e; `bun run check` = oxlint + tsc -b + bun test + app build) is a pull_request-event run on the exact current head SHA, and the extra `docs-build` leg appears only on #80 and #82 because docs.yml is path-filtered to packages/docs/** and only those two touch it. Total: 203 commits, 0 merge commits, no binary files, `207 files changed, 81122 insertions(+), 1394 deletions(-)` (packages+scripts 156 files +62403/−1276; .claude+docs 35 files +17241/−62; other 16 files +1478/−56). #69 is docs-only (26 files, +8361/−60), #84 is board/memory-only (5 files, +293/−8), and #77 is a one-commit stowaway fix to pre-existing store code (main's setPreferences already has the read-outside-write shape at packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts lines 497–503) that the board itself labels "a store fix, not M8"; it is tested by one test that reads the persisted document back and I ran it at the tip (1 pass). Nothing blocks merging bottom-up; the only findings are procedural: every PR shows BLOCKED/REVIEW_REQUIRED from the "main protected" ruleset (1 review + admin bypass), delete_branch_on_merge is off so each next PR must be retargeted to main by hand after its base merges, and the ruleset has no required-status-check rule so GitHub does not enforce CI.

items.text: fix(revud): a preference patch keeps the keys it never set; base m8.5/daemon-wiring, head prefs/lost-update
items.evidence: gh pr view 77: OPEN, base=m8.5/daemon-wiring (== #76 head), head=prefs/lost-update, headRefOid 6b29d91 == local == origin. rev-list head..base = 0, ahead 1 (the board's earlier 'forked at 0b32368, never picked up 048638c' drift is gone — 048638c is an ancestor). git diff --stat m8.5/daemon-wiring...prefs/lost-update: 2 files, +147/−13: packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts (setPreferences now does read+merge+upsert inside one `db.transaction(...)` committed via `tx.immediate()`, and throws 'the preferences transaction committed without merging a document' if the body never ran) and packages/revud/src/direct/store.test.ts. Test: `a preference patch made against a held write lock keeps the key it never set` inside describe `two connections writing at once: the loser waits and yields, never fails`; it spawns a real second process (holdWriteLock('prefs', ...)) that upserts {theme:'light',...} under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, calls store.setPreferences(LOCK_HOLDER_HUMAN, {diffMode:'split'}) while the lock is held, then asserts BOTH the returned document and the re-read `store.getPreferences(...)` carry diffMode 'split' AND theme 'light' — it reads the persisted row, and it pins an independent literal guard `expect(DEFAULT_PREFERENCES.theme).not.toBe('light')` so the discrimination cannot go vacuous. With the pre-fix shape (read outside the transaction) the WAL read returns the pre-holder state and the upsert writes theme back to the default, so the test goes red. Ran at the tip: `TZ=UTC bun test packages/revud/src/direct/store.test.ts -t 'preference patch'` → 1 pass, 0 fail, 5 expect() calls. The fix survives the 8 later chain commits that touch store.ts: at the tip `tx.immediate()` and the 'committed without merging' throw are still inside setPreferences (store.ts ~1644–1700). CI run 32301900094 (pull_request, sha 6b29d91, 2026-08-19): check/conformance-matrix/e2e pass.
items.note: Stowaway, deliberately and recorded: the buggy read-outside-write setPreferences already exists on main (git show main:packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts lines 497–503), so this fixes pre-existing code, not M8 code; BOARD.md line 141 and HANDOVER.md lines 781–784 label it 'a store fix, not M8'. It rides the chain because #73 (store v4) rewrote store.ts and a fix against main would not apply to v4. Merging it in order is correct; lifting it out would force a rebase of #78–#84.

gaps.title: No PR in the chain will auto-retarget after its base merges
gaps.detail: Repo setting delete_branch_on_merge=false (gh api repos/pat-mw/revu), so when #69 merges into main, #70 keeps base=m8/local-reviews-design and merging it would land on that branch, not main. Bottom-up order requires, after each merge, either retargeting the next PR's base to main or deleting the just-merged head branch (GitHub then retargets for you). The 'main protected' ruleset (id 19094308) has a `deletion` rule whose ref condition includes ~ALL, so only the bypass actor (RepositoryRole 5, bypass_mode always — the admin) can delete a chain branch. Because merge-base(main, tip) is main's own tip 177068a and main has not moved, every retargeted PR merges cleanly by construction as long as main stays put.
gaps.where: GitHub repo settings; ruleset 19094308 'main protected'; PR bases #70–#84

gaps.title: Merge method should be a merge commit, not squash/rebase, or each retargeted PR shows its predecessors' history
gaps.detail: The ruleset allows merge, squash and rebase. Squash or rebase-merge of #69 gives main a new SHA whose tree equals 8636b25 but which is not an ancestor of #70's branch; after retargeting, #70's PR view would show 19 commits (5 from #69 + its own 14) and a three-dot diff that includes #69's files. It stays MERGEABLE (identical changes on both sides), but the diff and commit list become misleading, and squashing 203 commits away loses the per-unit history the board and handover cite by SHA. Merging with a merge commit keeps every chain SHA and each subsequent PR shows only its own commits.
gaps.where: ruleset 19094308 allowed_merge_methods; merge UI choice per PR

gaps.title: All fifteen PRs are BLOCKED / REVIEW_REQUIRED with no non-admin merge path
gaps.detail: Every PR reports mergeable=MERGEABLE but mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED, reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED. Ruleset 19094308 applies to ~DEFAULT_BRANCH and ~ALL, requires required_approving_review_count=1 and require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes=true (all 203 commits carry a Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> trailer, author/committer pmassowalsh@gmail.com). No review of any kind exists on any of the fifteen PRs. The bypass actor (RepositoryRole 5, always) is the only merge path, which matches the recorded 'main merges via an admin-only ruleset' arrangement; it is not a defect, but anyone other than that admin cannot merge the chain.
gaps.where: ruleset 19094308 pull_request rule; gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision on #69–#84

gaps.title: CI is green but not enforced: the ruleset has no required_status_checks rule
gaps.detail: Ruleset 19094308's rules are deletion, non_fast_forward and pull_request only; there is no required_status_checks entry, so GitHub would allow a merge with a red or absent `check` run. Today every PR's check/conformance-matrix/e2e run is a pull_request-event success on the exact current head SHA (run ids 31622219936 … 33667507436, all conclusion=success), so nothing is at risk right now; but the merger must eyeball CI on each PR rather than rely on the merge button. This is a known, recorded deferral per the project memory, listed here only so the bottom-up merger does not assume the button checks it.

gaps.title: m8.3 and m8.4 branches are checked out in stale scratchpad worktrees
gaps.detail: `git worktree list` shows m8.3/local-snapshot-builder (2044c62) and m8.4/local-write-sink (21991fd) checked out at /private/tmp/claude-501/.../a3757a9b-.../scratchpad/wt-m83 and wt-m84, both marked prunable; `git branch` shows them with a `+` marker. Nothing is pending on them (behind-base is 0 for both), so this does not block merging; it would only refuse a future `git rebase`/checkout of those two branches from the main clone until `git worktree prune` is run.
gaps.where: git worktree list; branches m8.3/local-snapshot-builder, m8.4/local-write-sink

gaps.title: The `UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation)` constraint has no pin of its own
gaps.detail: R-A rules that the `generation` discriminator "stays in the unique key" and the ticket's Landmines call the UNIQUE constraint the mint's "real serializer". The DDL carries it (store.ts `CREATE_LOCAL_REVIEWS`), but no test reads `PRAGMA index_list('local_reviews')`, no test captures `sqlite_master.sql` for `local_reviews`, and no test drives a raw duplicate INSERT expecting `UNIQUE constraint failed` (grep for `UNIQUE`/`index_list`/`constraint failed` in store.test.ts and draft-isolation.test.ts finds none). `PRAGMA table_info` — what Check (2) pins — does not report UNIQUE indexes. Because `createLocalReview` dedupes through `selectLocalReview` under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before the INSERT ever conflicts, 'the same repo and branch pair mints once' and 'two live stores over one data dir mint one review for one branch pair' both stay green with the UNIQUE clause deleted from the DDL. The ticket's own Check (2) only demanded the column pin, so this is untested rather than missing; the mint's immediate transaction makes the constraint a second line of defence today.

gaps.title: local-git.ts normalizeRef has no production caller; the create path uses the shared validator
gaps.detail: M8.3.1's Do/Check specify normalizeRef(input, kind) as the seam's rejection-then-qualification step, and local-git.test.ts's 11-row rejection table (plus the Verify §3 injection gate) is written against it. On this tree the only callers of normalizeRef are tests: grep over packages for 'normalizeRef(' outside *.test.ts finds only its definition. The daemon's create path (packages/revud/src/direct/local-surface.ts qualifyRef, per M8.5.2's Check which names M8.1.2's isValidRefName) runs isValidRefName -> normalizeRefName from packages/shared/src/lib/refs.ts, then checkRefFormat. Consequences: (1) the M8.3.1 rejection table would stay green if the production validator lost its leading-dash rule — production rejection is pinned instead by packages/shared/src/lib/refs.test.ts 'rejects an argument-shaped name beginning with a dash', direct-router.test.ts HOSTILE_REFS (zero-invocation + positive control) and local-surface.test.ts 'refuses a ref name that would be read as an option', so the seed's clause holds; (2) normalizeRef's foreign-namespace rule is not enforced in production — qualifyRef accepts any refs/-prefixed name (e.g. refs/tags/v1 as a side, or a refs/remotes/… head) because normalizeRefName passes refs/* through unchanged and the picker's kind discriminator is not checked server-side. Not an injection risk (a refs/-qualified string cannot begin with '-'). Neither the M8.3 ticket, the board nor the handover records that the seam's normalizer was superseded by the shared one.
gaps.where: packages/revud/src/direct/local-git.ts normalizeRef; packages/revud/src/direct/local-surface.ts qualifyRef; packages/shared/src/lib/refs.ts isValidRefName/normalizeRefName; packages/revud/src/direct/local-git.test.ts HOSTILE_ROWS

audits.label: Ticket M8.5
audits.summary: Audited M8.5 (daemon wiring) against the seed in docs/agent/MILESTONES.md, the ticket's ten units, its Verify section and its six settled Open questions, reading the code on this tree and the body of every test cited. All ten units are implemented and each Check is pinned by tests that read the state they claim (spy call lists, thrown ApiError codes, raw SQLite rows, byte-literal messages, a child process that genuinely holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE) and carry a positive/negative control in the same file. The seed's four sub-bullets hold, with one recorded deviation: "threads" is deliberately NOT dispatched to a local implementation — GET /api/pulls/<localId>/threads stays 501 on both bands by design (Landmines + Verify), because local threads ride the snapshot's mutable half. The seed's Verify clauses are proven: local-reviews-serve.test.ts drives create→sync→draft→submit→reply→resolve→head_moved over real HTTP against a child revud in a remote-less repo under a --preload fetch tripwire; the four GitHub-PR suites, mode-select.test.ts, api-router.ts and dev-gate.test.ts are byte-identical from the PR base through HEAD; the 501 gates are re-pinned. Every owner ruling (OQ1 explicit switch, OQ3 rate-limit 501, OQ4 merged ETag, OQ5 LocalReviewSurface seam, OQ6 no CLI path) has an implementing unit, and OQ6's follow-up is recorded in HANDOVER/LOG. PR #76 is OPEN on m8.4/local-write-sink with CI green (check, conformance-matrix, e2e). Only minor gaps: the serve suite does not clear GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN from the child env (structurally moot), the tripwire's own firing has no durable control, and the OQ6 CLI follow-up lives in HANDOVER/LOG rather than BOARD.

gaps.title: Serve suite does not clear GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN from the child daemon's environment
gaps.detail: The ticket's M8.5.7 Check says the suite is green 'with no gh, no token and no origin', but CLEARED_ENV_KEYS in packages/revud/src/local-reviews-serve.test.ts (:207-214) lists REVU_MODE/REVU_REPO/REVU_ROLE/REVU_BOT_LOGIN/REVU_LOCAL_ONLY/REVU_CREDENTIALS_FILE and the child inherits `{...process.env}`, so a developer or CI shell carrying GH_TOKEN would pass it through. Structurally moot on this tree: with no origin the token source is never consulted (context.ts:287 `validateToken = requireGithub || repo !== undefined` → false) and the --preload tripwire would name any fetch — but 'no token' is currently a property of the code path, not something the fixture guarantees.

gaps.title: The fetch tripwire's own firing has no durable control in the suite
gaps.detail: local-reviews-serve.test.ts spawns the child under `bun --preload no-network-preload.ts`, and the ticket's negative control (point a route at deps.github.getRateLimit() and watch the tripwire fail the suite) was run once and recorded in ## Log. Nothing in the tree asserts that the preload actually replaced fetch inside the child (e.g. a probe that makes the daemon call fetch and observes the named failure), so a future Bun that changed --preload semantics would leave the suite green while the tripwire silently stopped guarding. The ticket's 'Testing exceptions' section names this as belt-to-braces rather than the proof, and the D7 import-graph and throwing-client proofs stand independently.

gaps.title: Branch listing is refreshed on reopen only past a 10 s staleTime, not 'when the dialog opens'
gaps.detail: M8.6.2's Do says branches are 'refetched when the create dialog opens', and the Log justifies staleTime 10_000 + refetchOnMount 'always' 'for a body that mounts on open'. After M8.6.5 lifted the dialog into the shell it is mounted once and useBranches({ enabled: open }) never remounts, so refetchOnMount never fires on reopen; the enabled false→true transition refetches only when the entry is stale (TanStack v5 shouldFetchOptionally → isStale). Reopening within 10 s offers the previous listing. The hook's docstring ('refetches whenever a fresh observer mounts') describes the pre-lift wiring. Untested either way (hook).

audits.summary: Audited M8.8 against the seed (MILESTONES.md §Issue M8.8), the ticket's eight units and eight Verify clauses, and PR #78 (OPEN, base prefs/lost-update, head m8.8/resync-and-pinning, not merged; checks: check pass, conformance-matrix pass, e2e pass, Vercel pass). All eight units have code on the tree and non-vacuous tests: local-pins.ts (atomic update-ref --stdin, ref-legality proven against real git), performSync in local-surface.ts pins before the first object read (ordering asserted with a >= 0 guard), reconcile.ts and the mock adapter both report the whole compare when the draft head is absent (the old author-date subset is computed inline and asserted strictly smaller, reporting zero on the fixture), the hasBlob pre-flight plus the rebuildable() edge mapping turn missing objects into a typed not_found whose remedy is asserted to work, a deleted/renamed branch loses no draft under a runtime deletion tripwire with a permanent negative control, the prune-survival pair (reflog expire + gc --prune=now) has a control that goes red without the pin, and reconcile-plan/withDraftHead/setHead move headSha and compareKey together before the submit. All three seed Verify clauses are proven; the owner's ruling on OQ4 (keep every pin, no delete export, M8.10 in the same session) is implemented (local-pins.ts exports no delete; M8.10 is #79 based on the M8.8 branch). Two shortfalls: M8.8.3's third Check bullet (a parity leg importing createMockApi into reconcile.test.ts so mock and revud are asserted identical on newCommits for the rewritten fixture) was never written — the two transports are pinned by independent tests and the conformance reconcile fixture keeps the draft head present, so ticket Verify 7 is only partially proven; and the seed's "review read-only" clause for a deleted head is enforced only incidentally by resolveLocalHead's typed refusal on the write path, which no test drives against a deleted branch and no app surface renders. Both targeted runs were green (reconcile.test.ts 13/13, reconcile-plan.test.ts 15/15).

gaps.title: M8.8.3's real-mock parity leg was never written (ticket Verify 7)
gaps.detail: The unit's third Check bullet and Verify clause 7 require reconcile.test.ts to import createMockApi/mockDev from @revu/app/mock, sync a mock PR, save a draft whose headSha is absent from the snapshot's commits, and assert revud's and the mock's newCommits agree — explicitly 'not by replaying a transcription of the mock's body'. On this tree reconcile.test.ts imports no createMockApi (only packages/revud/src/mock-bridge.ts and failure-drills.test.ts do), oracleResults() still replays classification only, and the transports are pinned by two independent tests (reconcile.test.ts 'reports every commit when the draft head fell out of the rewritten compare' with a fake store; packages/app/src/api/mock/local.test.ts 'a rebase reports every commit as new, because the draft head is gone' and reconcile-plan.test.ts 'a stale head reports the whole branch as new; the moved head reports none' on the mock). The shared conformance reconcile case (packages/shared/conformance/suite.ts ~322-351) keeps the draft head present and expects 3 newCommits, so no matrix leg covers the head-absent branch either. The ticket's M8.8.3 Log entry acknowledges this ('asserted by two independent tests rather than by one oracle. Worth closing when the parity unit lands') but no unit closed it and no deviation reason is recorded; the ticket's Verify-run record lists only items 1-5.
gaps.where: packages/revud/src/direct/reconcile.test.ts (oracleResults, no createMockApi import); packages/shared/conformance/suite.ts reconcile case; ticket M8.8.3 Check bullet 3, Verify 7

gaps.title: Seed's 'review read-only' after a deleted/renamed branch is neither pinned nor rendered
gaps.detail: Seed bullet 4 promises 'typed not_found, review read-only, drafts and threads preserved'. The typed error and preservation are proven (local-resync.test.ts). Read-only is only incidental: the write verbs resolve the head through resolveLocalHead (packages/revud/src/direct/local-surface.ts ~361-372), which throws ApiError('not_found', '...The branch has been deleted or renamed...') when rev-parse fails — but no test drives a submit/reply against a deleted branch (grep for 'rev-parse exited' / 'deleted or renamed' in *.test.ts hits only a fixture helper in local-archive-sync.test.ts), and no app surface derives or renders a read-only state from the sync's not_found (packages/app read-only handling exists only for the archived-by-PR case in review-bar.tsx / review-mode.ts). The ticket re-scoped read-only as 'derived, not stored' (M8.8.5 Do) without saying what enforces it.

gaps.detail: Open question 2 says the shared reconcile change 'Needs sign-off before M8.8.3 lands, because the test rewrite is the point of no return'. reconcile.ts changed the hosted PR path and reconcile.test.ts's author-date test was rewritten; LOG.md:174 recommends 'yes' and the ticket Log calls it deliberate, but the board's rulings table (rulings 1-5) contains no M8.8 OQ2 ruling and the question is still open text in the ticket. The behaviour matches seed bullet 2, so this is documentation only.

gaps.title: The 'base advanced — diff changed' banner cannot fire for a local review in direct mode
gaps.detail: M8.8.6 says its job is 'to prove it fires for a local review'. The daemon-level proof exists (local-resync.test.ts 'the head is byte-identical and the compare key is not') and the D8 tooltip is present and guarded, but useStaleness (packages/app/src/state/queries.ts:183-198) compares item.broker.compareKey with the stored snapshot's compareKey, and revud's local list row derives broker.compareKey from the stored review row (direct-api.ts localCompareKey: review.mergeBaseSha...review.headSha), which the same sync stamps — so stale is never true for a local review between syncs and the banner (pr-layout.tsx:235) is unreachable in direct mode; only the reconcile dialog's zero-commit copy surfaces a base advance. The mock's listLocalPullRows (packages/app/src/api/mock/local.ts ~381-399) reads live ref tips instead (with mergeBaseSha = headSha), a list-row divergence between the spec and revud that belongs to M8.5.3's listPulls merge rather than to M8.8.
gaps.where: packages/revud/src/direct/direct-api.ts localCompareKey/localPullListItem; packages/app/src/state/queries.ts useStaleness; packages/app/src/api/mock/local.ts listLocalPullRows

gaps.title: M8.8.7's 'tsc-level row' for the paired head signature is absent
gaps.detail: The Check asks for a tsc-level row (e.g. an @ts-expect-error call passing headSha without compareKey) plus a runtime assertion that compareKey ends with headSha. Only the runtime row exists (reconcile-plan.test.ts 'moves the SHA and the compare key together and leaves the rest alone'); DraftHead's two required fields make the inconsistent call a type error in practice, but nothing in the gate would notice if compareKey became optional.

audits.label: Ticket M8.9
audits.summary: Audited M8.9 (archive when a PR appears) on board/m8.9-scratch-proof: the seed's three sub-bullets and Verify line, all eight units of the ticket, every ticket Verify clause, and the ten Open-question rulings, against the code and tests on this tree. PR #82 is OPEN on base m8.11/conformance-e2e-docs with all six checks passing (check, conformance-matrix, e2e, docs-build, two Vercel); packages/shared/src/api/ and context.test.ts have no diff on the branch. Every seed sub-bullet, unit and Verify clause is implemented and pinned by non-vacuous tests: the shared predicate table (fork, base, blank identity, ref-shape rows), the detector's zero-request case with a fetch double and in-body positive control, the store's write-once/one-column/DELETE-allowlist gates with self-checks, the four write refusals with byte-identical serialization before and after plus live controls, the sweep driven through the real syncPull on a real fixture (one match, one lower-numbered fork, exactly one archived), closed-without-merge with an open sibling archiving in the same run, the freeze with a moved-head control, the ETag pins on direct-api and the router (304 bodiless, then 200 with the row still present and closed), the banner as real HTML with its empty render and control, and the three-transport conformance block (E/F/G). One recorded deviation (M8.9.5 shrank to pins because M8.5 already hashed the whole row) is reasoned in the Log; M8.9.1's predicate moved to packages/shared with the reason recorded. What does not fully hold is minor: OQ2's ruling asked that "a review nobody re-syncs stays un-archived" be carried into UI copy, and it lands only in the guide (no live-review UI copy says detection runs on sync); and mainBroker's seam wiring (pairListingFor over pollClient) has no test or walk, while mainDirect's is corroborated live by the scratch proof. OQ10 (draft writable on an archived review) is open and recorded on the board as the owner's call, not a gap.

audits.label: Exit criterion 1
audits.summary: Exit criterion 1 is PROVEN on this tree, by code and tests rather than by board sentences. Every clause has at least two independent proofs: the shared suite packages/shared/conformance/local-suite.ts (run as required matrix legs E mock / F revud-mock HTTP / G direct engine over a zero-remote seeded repo under a fetch tripwire), the real-daemon HTTP suite packages/revud/src/local-reviews-serve.test.ts (child revud under a --preload fetch tripwire in a no-remote repo, with restart and a real git --amend), and the browser e2e e2e/local-review.ts (tokens emptied, GH_CONFIG_DIR absent, netlog guard with an installed marker). Structurally, local-surface.ts hands provisionBlobs no github/repo so blobs.ts tier 3 cannot execute, context.ts:287 never consults the token source when no origin parses under requireGithub:false, and direct-api.ts dispatches every id-keyed method to the local surface before any GithubClient read (pinned by direct-api.test.ts with a positive control). I ran leg G with GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN unset: 38 pass, 0 fail; gh reports check, conformance-matrix and e2e all passing on #84 at 7403f3b, which equals the local HEAD. Two minor weaknesses, neither a gap: local-reviews-serve.test.ts:468 asserts syncStats.requests === 0 but local-surface.ts:800 hardcodes that literal (decorative), and that suite has no positive control that its --preload tripwire loaded (leg G and the e2e do have one).

audits.label: Exit criterion 2
audits.summary: Criterion 2 splits into four clauses; on this tree two are proven and two are partially proven, so the criterion as a whole is PARTIALLY PROVEN, not proven as the board says. The amend clause and the "never mass-classifies as lost through unreachable objects" clause are held by real assertions that would go red if the behaviour were removed: local-resync.test.ts runs a real `git commit --amend` + reflog expire + `gc --prune=now` + `DELETE FROM blobs` walk and asserts zero `lost` over a real 3-comment draft, the pinned/unpinned object-survival pair has a genuine control (the old head commit is collected when `update-ref` is swallowed), local-surface.test.ts pins the pin argv strictly before the first `diff`/`cat-file`, and reconcile.test.ts proves a missing anchor blob is a typed `not_found` and is never classified (with a genuine-`lost` negative control in the same file); the author-date fallback is gone from revud/shared production code and both revud and the mock carry a strictly-worse inline guard. The "new commits" clause is proven only compositionally for local reviews: the shared engine's after-head slicing is pinned (reconcile.test.ts, conformance-reconcile.test.ts, the PR-path conformance suite), and a live local review is shown to follow a new head commit on re-sync, but no test walks sync -> draft -> new head commit -> re-sync -> reconcile on a local review, and the local conformance legs E/F/G contain no `reconcileDraft` call at all. Three of its four named clauses are proven by code plus tests that read real values: the tab omission is asserted on rendered PrTabs markup (packages/app/src/pages/pr-layout.test.ts), on the route guard and tab table (packages/app/src/lib/review-mode.test.ts), and live in a headless Chrome against a local-only direct daemon (e2e/local-review.ts, run by the CI `e2e` job); the lock is gated by showSelfReviewLock with its predicate, import and single canApprove read pinned; the toast is pinned to "Review saved — N comments on this branch." with /API call/ and /posted/ banned across every copy export and every scanned chrome file, and the e2e waits for the "Review saved" toast on a real submit. The rate-limit clause is proven for the three cost sentences (seal tooltip, never-synced hint, sync-error fallback) but the topbar rate chip is a RECORDED DEVIATION: ruling R2 in the M8.7 ticket makes the chip workspace-scoped, so on a local review in a GitHub-capable workspace the chip and its budget tooltip still render; in a local-only workspace its omission rests on the daemon's 501 (pinned in packages/revud/src/local-reviews-serve.test.ts) plus an app-shell.tsx derivation that no test reads. audits.label: Design §3 Decisions and §3.1 id bands
audits.summary: Audited docs/agent/LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §3 (D1–D8), §3.1 and §9 against the working tree at the tip of the fifteen-PR stack (#84 OPEN, nothing merged), plus the user guide, the run-modes pages and docs/security-review.md. Every design decision D1–D8 is implemented and pinned by named tests, most on all three local conformance legs (E mock in-process, F revud-mock over HTTP, G direct engine) via packages/shared/conformance/local-suite.ts and local-archive.ts. Two §3.1 statements deviate from the code by recorded owner rulings (M8.2 R-A/R-B: the unique key carries a `generation` column and ids come from a monotonic high-water mark, never `MAX(id)+1`) and one D3 detail deviates by ruling (M8.3 R-B: dirty is `git status --porcelain=v1 -uno`, so untracked files raise no banner) — the design doc and the guide were not updated to say so. §9 holds: nothing crosses workspaces, nothing publishes, nothing reviews uncommitted work, no shared database, and no later ticket delivered something §9 rules out. No user-facing sentence was found that the code contradicts; the only open behavioural question is M8.9 OQ10 (a draft PUT still succeeds on an archived review), recorded but unruled. No blocker or major gap; five minor doc-drift items.

gaps.title: §3.1 and §4.2 still describe MAX(id)+1 minting and a three-column UNIQUE key
gaps.detail: LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §3.1 promises 'UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref) plus MAX(id) + 1 minting' and §4.2's DDL has no generation column. The code (packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts) has UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation) and mints from the `local_review_id_high_water` meta row, explicitly 'not MAX(id) + 1'. The deviation is ruled and reasoned in tickets/M8.2-store-v4.md R-A/R-B (2026-08-14) and pinned by store.test.ts 'deleting a review does not move the high-water mark backwards' and 'the removed id is never minted again…'; the design doc was never amended.

gaps.title: D3 dirty detection excludes untracked files; neither the design nor the guide says so
gaps.detail: D3 says `git status --porcelain` drives the banner (default output includes `??` rows); the guide says any edit sitting in the working tree is outside the review and dirty trees get a banner. local-sync.ts:1500 runs `--porcelain=v1 -uno`, pinned by local-sync.test.ts 'an uncommitted change is what makes a worktree dirty, and an untracked file is not one'. So an uncommitted new file is excluded from the review and raises no banner. Ruled in tickets/M8.3-local-snapshot-builder.md R-B (and M8.2 R-C); the docs do not carry the exclusion.

gaps.title: D5 says 'direct/broker mode'; only direct mode carries the capability
gaps.detail: The capability is wired in mainDirect only (packages/revud/src/index.ts); run-modes/index.mdx correctly says 'a capability inside direct mode alone' and that no broker boot ships yet. The design's 'direct/broker' phrasing is wider than what exists. No ticket records a broker-mode deferral for local reviews because the broker boot itself is not shipped.

gaps.title: D1 'read-only' leaves the draft writable on an archived review (M8.9 OQ10, unruled)
gaps.detail: The four write verbs refuse (conformance local-archive.ts 'the four write verbs refuse, before touching anything'), but the conformance suite also pins that a draft edit still saves on an archived review, and the scratch-repo walk found the inline gutter composer still opens with PUT draft answering 200. tickets/M8.9-archive-on-pr.md OQ10 records this as the owner's call with either answer being one unit; the guide §7 does not say drafts remain editable. Not a correctness defect — nothing reaches GitHub either way.
gaps.where: tickets/M8.9-archive-on-pr.md OQ10; packages/shared/conformance/local-archive.ts 'reads and drafts stay open on an archived review'; packages/app review bar / gutter composer

gaps.title: D2 overstates the mock router's gate
gaps.detail: D2 and §3.1 say both routers require `Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0`. The direct router does (direct-router.ts:259); the mock router's intParam (packages/revud/src/api-router.ts:118) checks only Number.isInteger, identically on main. A wording inaccuracy in the design, not an M8 regression, and the local id band is positive regardless.

audits.label: Design §4 Data model
audits.summary: Audited LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §4 (4.1 what is synthesized, 4.2 store schema v3→v4) plus §9 against the working tree on board/m8.9-scratch-proof, and spot-checked the local-review guide, the run-modes pages and docs/security-review.md. Every §4.1 field has a legal local value in both producers (revud `synthesizeLocalPullDetail` in packages/revud/src/direct/local-sync.ts, mock `synthesizePullDetail` in packages/app/src/api/mock/local.ts) and all but `mutable.checks` are pinned by named tests; §4.2's six tables, additive ladder, `STORE_VERSION = 4`, D4 containment, repo scoping and per-human draft isolation are implemented in packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts and pinned in store.test.ts, draft-isolation.test.ts and local-reviews-serve.test.ts. Two schema-level deviations from the §4.2/§3.1 text are recorded owner rulings in M8.2 (R-A: a `generation` column and a four-column UNIQUE key; R-B: monotonic high-water marks in `meta` instead of `MAX(id)+1`), and the dirty flag uses `-uno` under M8.3's R-B; the design doc itself was never amended, so it is stale on those three points. §9's four non-goals all hold and none was later delivered by a ticket. No user-facing doc sentence contradicts the code; the guide's archive detector, dialog copy, chord, inbox ordering and security-review file references all exist as described. No blocker or major gaps; the findings are doc drift and one untested empty field.

audits.label: Design §5 Building a local snapshot, §5.1 pinning
audits.summary: Audited docs/agent/LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §5 (Building a local snapshot) and §5.1 (Object pinning) against the working tree at the tip of the fifteen-PR stack, reading the builder (packages/revud/src/direct/local-sync.ts, local-git.ts), the pin module (local-pins.ts), the blob ladder (blobs.ts), the sync orchestrator (local-surface.ts), retention.ts, and their suites, and running local-pins.test.ts (22 pass). Every behavioural promise in the two sections is implemented and pinned by a named test that reads real git output or a recording runner and would go red if the behaviour were removed: rev-parse/merge-base/--raw --no-abbrev -M/--numstat/--unified=3/log over merge-base..head, no 3000-file cap, absent-patch-means-no-text-diff, the 8000-byte NUL sniff, a structurally absent GitHub tier, a pin written before the first object read on every live sync, objects surviving an aggressive gc with an unpinned control, and eviction as an explicit ref drop on delete. Three promises deviate in mechanism from the design's wording and each deviation is recorded in a ticket log with its reason: the pin ref is `refs/revu/reviews/<id>/<mergeBase>-<head>/{base,head}` because a compareKey containing `..` is not a legal ref name (M8.8.1); provisionBlobs has no local-only flag, the hosted client is an omitted dependency (M8.3.6); and a frozen archived sync attempts no pin (M8.9 OQ9, decided 2026-09-02). The user-facing docs (local-review.mdx, run-modes/direct.mdx, run-modes/index.mdx, concepts/compare-key.mdx, docs/security-review.md) contain no present-tense sentence the code contradicts, and §9's four non-goals still hold with nothing later delivered against them. Gaps are all minor doc drift: the design still spells the literal `<compareKey>` ref, still says "one flag", still describes the missing-object degradation that a typed not_found pre-flight now intercepts, and its header still says the Linear board carries the units; the one open behavioural residue is that a failed pin is reported on the sync outcome and rendered nowhere (M8.8 OQ3, unanswered).

gaps.title: §5.1 still spells the pin ref as refs/revu/reviews/<id>/<compareKey>, which git cannot create
gaps.detail: The design's literal name contains the compareKey's `...`, and git rejects any ref name containing `..`. The implementation writes two refs, refs/revu/reviews/<id>/<mergeBase>-<head>/base and /head, in one update-ref --stdin batch; the reason and the measured check-ref-format exit are recorded in the M8.8.1 unit text and pinned by local-pins.test.ts "the design's literal compare-key form is rejected, which is why the substitution exists". The design doc was never updated.

gaps.title: §5 says provisionBlobs gains 'one flag' for local-only; the code omits the client instead
gaps.detail: There is no flag. blobs.ts makes github/repo optional dependencies and the local sync path (local-surface.ts:740) passes neither, so the hosted tier is structurally absent. The choice and its rationale ('an absent client is a stronger statement than a flag') are recorded in the M8.3.6 log entry and in the blobs.ts docstring; the behaviour (never fall back) is what the design wanted. Only the design wording is stale.

gaps.title: §5.1 describes the missing-object degradation (null → lost/line-deleted) that the code no longer performs
gaps.detail: M8.8.4 added a reconcile pre-flight: when any anchor blob is absent from the store the reconcile refuses with a typed not_found naming a re-sync rather than classifying anything, and the API edge maps a missing immutable half to the same answer. §5.1 still presents mass-`lost` as the live failure mode with pinning as the only mitigation. Pinned by reconcile.test.ts 'nothing is classified when an object is missing' and local-objects-missing.test.ts 'the edge answers a re-syncable not_found, not a corrupt daemon'.

gaps.title: A failed pin is reported on the sync outcome and rendered nowhere
gaps.detail: §5.1 promises a pin on every local sync. When update-ref fails the sync still succeeds (correct, and tested: 'a failed pin is not a failed sync, and is reported'), but the outcome lands only in LocalSyncOutcome.pin, which no route or UI surfaces, so a review with no retention guarantee looks identical to a pinned one. This is M8.8 Open question 3 ('Where does a failed pin surface?'), recorded as open and deliberately not folded into `partial`; no owner ruling yet.

audits.label: Design §6 Writes
audits.summary: Audited docs/agent/LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §6 Writes (plus §8 "Writes" cases 17-19, D7, and §9) against the tree at board/m8.9-scratch-proof. Every concrete §6 promise is implemented in packages/revud/src/direct/local-writes.ts (sink), local-surface.ts (wiring: git rev-parse head guard, port built member-by-member), the mock oracle packages/app/src/api/mock/local.ts, and the app side (state/threads.ts optimisticBody/optimisticResolvedBy, lib/review-mode.ts showSelfReviewLock, lib/mode-copy.ts), and each is pinned by named tests in local-writes.test.ts (142 pass / 0 fail when run in isolation), local-ids.test.ts, local-write-isolation.test.ts, local-surface.test.ts, local-reviews-serve.test.ts (real git over HTTP), and the shared local conformance suite run as matrix legs E/F/G. The only unpinned §6 clause is the structural "conflict is unreachable locally" (true by inspection: the string never appears in the sink; ApiErrorCode keeps the code), and the two deliberately dropped steps (idempotency re-check, 422 path) are absences recorded in M8.4's ticket with the accepted resubmit-duplicates cost. The mock-vs-revud disagreement on head_moved.newCommits (constant 0 vs a compare-scoped count) is a recorded M8.1 ruling, not a §6 promise. No user-facing doc sentence in local-review.mdx, run-modes/*.mdx or docs/security-review.md contradicts the code; §9's four won't-dos all still hold and no later ticket delivered any of them. Gaps found are minor: D5's "direct/broker" wording in the design doc versus a direct-only wiring, and M8.4's ticket text saying the forbidden variant is never returned after M8.9 made it the archive refusal.

items.text: Each local write verb returns a complete, well-formed value; a no-op that returns the old value makes the optimistic update snap back.

audits.label: Design §7 Frontend
audits.summary: Audited docs/agent/LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §7 Frontend (with the frontend-facing sentences of §3.1 and the tail of §6) against the working tree at board/m8.9-scratch-proof, plus the local-review guide, the run-modes pages and docs/security-review.md, and §9. Every §7 promise is implemented: the /pr/:n route family is untouched with a single digits-only matcher, the whole variance is one ReviewMode derived from the app's single reading-side call to the band predicate (pinned by a source scan), Checks/Description are omitted and their routes redirect, Conversation is threads-only, the create flow offers every ref as a base and local branches as a head, and every harmful string in the inventory is answered by a pure copy function pinned in both modes plus a residual sweep over the chrome. Two §7 statements were deliberately overridden by recorded owner rulings (the rate chip is workspace-scoped, not suppressed on a local review — M8.7 R2; the inbox section renders empty below everything else when the reader holds local reviews but none is visible — M8.6 R1). No D-decision or exit-criterion behaviour is unmet and §9 is not contradicted by anything the code does. What does not hold is minor: the guide says the Local reviews section drops below every other section once all are closed, but an archived row keeps it at the top (visibleRows keeps closed local items; the only 'below' test uses no local rows at all); the guide's 'goes read-only' is softened by M8.9 OQ10 (gutter composer and draft PUT still accepted on an archived review, recorded open); the palette Go entry and the shell-side g l registration have no test; D5 and an index.ts comment say 'direct/broker' while only mainDirect builds the local surface (the user docs correctly say direct alone).

audits.label: Design §8 Edge cases — Creation, Re-sync
audits.summary: Audited docs/agent/LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §8 Creation (cases 1–10) and Re-sync (cases 11–16) against the tree at board/m8.9-scratch-proof, plus the user docs for this area and §9. Fifteen of the sixteen cases are implemented and pinned by named tests in packages/revud/src/direct (local-git, local-sync, local-surface, local-resync, local-pins, local-objects-missing), the mock (packages/app/src/api/mock/local*.test.ts), the shared conformance suite and the app (create-local-review, dirty-banner, reconcile-copy). One concrete promise does not hold: case 13's "compareKey changes → baseMoved". The app derives staleness from the list row's compareKey and head sha (packages/app/src/state/queries.ts useStaleness), but for a local review both come from the stored row stamped by the same sync that wrote the snapshot (direct-api.ts localCompareKey / localPullListItem, and the mock's local.ts:555 does the same), so a local review can never show "base advanced — diff changed" or "N new commits since sync" before a Re-sync; M8.5.3 specified the row-derived key while M8.8 assumed a "live list row", and no ruling reconciles them. The guide's "the review can go stale ... with zero new commits on the head" over-claims on the same point. Cases 4 and 5 (unrelated histories, shallow clone) are detected at first sync rather than at create, which the design lists under Creation. §9 is intact: nothing in the code crosses workspaces, publishes, reviews uncommitted work, or shares a database.

items.text: Unrelated histories, no merge base → typed error naming the two refs.
items.evidence: local-sync.ts resolveLocalRange: merge-base exit 1 + empty stdout + not shallow → { reason: 'unrelated_histories', baseRef, headRef }; local-surface.ts rangeRefusal → ApiError('unprocessable') whose message names both refs. Tests: local-sync.test.ts 'two refs with no common ancestor in a complete repository yields unrelated_histories' (asserts both refs on the failure), 'the two no-common-ancestor rows differ only in the shallow probe', 'git reports the missing ancestor exactly as it reports unrelated histories' (real git). Caveats: only reachable at first sync — createLocalReview resolves no SHAs by design (local-surface.ts comment; local-surface.test.ts 'resolves no SHAs at create — the review starts unsynced'), so the create dialog never shows it (create-local-review.test.ts 'names both refs when the histories are unrelated' feeds a hand-written message); the surface-level ApiError message text for this case is not asserted anywhere.

items.text: Shallow clone → git merge-base can fail; detect and say so rather than reporting an empty diff.
items.evidence: local-sync.ts isShallowRepository probe (rev-parse --is-shallow-repository) runs before reporting unrelated_histories; rangeRefusal 'shallow_clone' → unprocessable telling the user to deepen the clone. Tests: local-sync.test.ts 'the identical merge-base outcome in a shallow clone yields shallow_clone', and the real-clone leg 'git really does report the clone as shallow', 'the resolver reports the clone rather than the histories'. Same caveat as §8.4: detected at first sync, not at create.

items.text: Duplicate (repo, base, head) → returns the existing review; the UNIQUE constraint enforces it.
items.evidence: packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts createLocalReview: lookup then INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation) DO NOTHING inside a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, returning the winning row. items.text: Ref names over HTTP are option-injection vectors: normalize to refs/heads/…, pass --, and validate with git check-ref-format.

items.text: Repo root is never discovered today; worktrees and bare repos need git rev-parse --show-toplevel.

items.text: Submodule (160000) and symlink (120000) entries in git diff --raw → skipped or explicitly marked, not fed to the blob provider.

items.text: New commits → new compareKey → new immutable half → reconcile; re-sync is literally syncPull, no new route.

items.text: Base advances with no head commits → merge base moves → compareKey changes → baseMoved. Correct under D8, and a real behavioral difference worth stating in the UI.
items.evidence: Server half holds: local-resync.test.ts 'the head is byte-identical and the compare key is not' (real git, base advanced only); local-sync.test.ts 'a commit on the base branch moves the base tip with no new head commit', 'a base advance reaching into the head history moves the compare key'. UI statement exists: pr-layout.tsx SnapshotSeal tooltip on the base-advanced branch names the live-tip vs pull.base.sha difference (untested — pr-layout.test.ts 'the base advanced' pins only the seal label, tooltip bodies are portal-rendered). The '→ baseMoved' half does not hold: packages/app/src/state/queries.ts useStaleness sets stale = item.broker.compareKey !== snapshot.immutable.compareKey and baseMoved = stale && item.pull.head.sha === snapshot headSha; for a local review the list row's compareKey is localCompareKey(review) = the stored row's mergeBaseSha...headSha and pull.head.sha is the row's headSha (direct-api.ts localPullListItem), both written by patchLocalReviewSync in the same sync that stored the snapshot, so stale is structurally false and baseMoved (and 'N new commits since sync') can never render before a Re-sync. The mock does the same (packages/app/src/api/mock/local.ts:555). No test asserts a local row goes stale without a sync. M8.5.3's Do specifies 'compareKey from the review row'; M8.8 (ticket lines 56–57, 318–319) assumed 'a live list row' — unreconciled, no ruling.

items.text: Head or base branch deleted or renamed → typed not_found; the review goes read-only; drafts and threads are never discarded.
items.evidence: local-surface.ts rangeRefusal 'ref_not_found' → ApiError('not_found') naming the ref; write verbs' live head resolution answers the same not_found; store reads never consult git. Tests: local-resync.test.ts 'the sync refuses with a typed answer naming the ref', 'the draft is byte-for-byte what it was', 'the threads are unchanged', 'the last good snapshot still opens', 'the review is still listed, so it can be read and deleted deliberately', 'the sync refuses and names the base ref' (git branch -m), deletion tripwire 'the failing sync completes its refusal without deleting anything' with negative control 'the same decorator does refuse a real deletion'; local-surface.test.ts 'a head branch deleted after the review was created answers a typed not-found naming the ref' (submit and reply refused, draft intact). 'Read-only' is derived from write refusal, not a stored state — M8.8.5 says so by design.

items.text: Repo re-cloned or data dir moved → a graceful 'objects missing, re-sync to rebuild' state instead of a hard unreadable error.
items.evidence: local-surface.ts rebuildable translates StoreUnreadableError on snapshot reads (getSnapshot, reconcileDraft, the write port) into ApiError('not_found') naming a re-sync; direct/reconcile.ts pre-flights anchor blobs via hasBlob and answers not_found naming a re-sync instead of mass 'lost'; store still throws. items.text: local-review.mdx: 'the review can go stale — and its compare key can move — with zero new commits on the head.'
items.evidence: The compare-key half is true (local-resync.test.ts 'the head is byte-identical and the compare key is not'). The 'go stale' half is contradicted by the code: useStaleness cannot turn the seal gold on a local review because the list row and the snapshot carry the same last-synced compareKey (see §8.13). concepts/compare-key.mdx and run-modes/index.mdx only claim the compare key moves, which is correct.

items.text: What this does not do: no cross-workspace review; no publishing local comments to a PR, ever (D1); no review of uncommitted work (D3); no shared database.
items.evidence: Nothing in the tree does any of the four: the local write path has no GitHub client or runner in its import graph (local-write-isolation.test.ts, local-no-github.test.ts 'no local module reaches for … a hosted forge'); detectDirtyWorktree only observes the worktree (local-sync.ts: 'observed, never taken into the review'); reviews live in the per-data-dir SQLite under the discovered repo identity (store.test.ts 'the same branch pair under two repositories are two distinct reviews'). No §9 bullet was later delivered by a ticket, so the section is not stale; the later additions (retention/GC in M8.10, delete in M8.10/M8.12, archive in M8.9) were anticipated by §8 cases 22–23, not excluded by §9.

gaps.title: A local review never goes stale before a Re-sync: baseMoved and 'N new commits since sync' are unreachable
gaps.detail: §8.13 promises base advance → compareKey changes → baseMoved, and §7/§8.11 rely on the staleness seal being 'correct as-is locally'. The app derives staleness in packages/app/src/state/queries.ts useStaleness from item.broker.compareKey vs snapshot.immutable.compareKey and item.pull.head.sha vs the snapshot head. For a local review the list row is built by direct-api.ts localPullListItem from the stored row: compareKey = localCompareKey(review) (the row's last-synced mergeBaseSha...headSha) and head.sha = review.headSha, both stamped by local-surface.ts patchLocalReviewSync in the same sync that stored the snapshot. So stale is always false, the seal never turns gold, and the D8 tooltip that states the difference is never shown. The mock (the spec) does the same at packages/app/src/api/mock/local.ts:555. No test asserts a local row goes stale without a sync; pr-layout.test.ts 'the base advanced' feeds a fabricated staleness report. M8.5.3's Do specified 'compareKey from the review row' while M8.8 (tickets/M8.8-resync-and-pinning.md lines 56–57 and 318–319) assumed 'a live list row' — the two tickets disagree and no owner ruling reconciles them. Reconcile after a manual Re-sync still works (local-resync.test.ts), so the loss is the pre-sync signal, not the re-anchoring.
gaps.where: packages/revud/src/direct/direct-api.ts localCompareKey / localPullListItem; packages/app/src/api/mock/local.ts:555; packages/app/src/state/queries.ts useStaleness; packages/app/src/pages/pr-layout.tsx SnapshotSeal; tickets M8.5.3 vs M8.8.6

gaps.title: Guide over-claims that a local review 'can go stale' with zero head commits
gaps.detail: packages/docs/content/docs/guides/local-review.mdx §5 says 'the review can go stale — and its compare key can move — with zero new commits on the head'. The compare key does move (tested); the seal cannot go gold on a local review (see the major gap). Downstream of that gap; the sentence should say the next sync reflects the base advance rather than that the review goes stale.

gaps.title: Unrelated histories and shallow clone are detected at first sync, not at creation
gaps.detail: §8 lists cases 4 and 5 under Creation, but createLocalReview deliberately resolves no SHAs (local-surface.ts comment; local-surface.test.ts 'resolves no SHAs at create'), so both typed errors surface only when the review is first synced; the create dialog lands the user on the review and the sync reports them. The behaviour is sound and tested (local-sync.test.ts rows and the real shallow-clone leg), but the design doc's placement is not updated and no ticket records the move as a deviation; the app's create-error test for 'unrelated histories' exercises a hand-written message the server never sends at create.
gaps.where: docs/agent/LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §8 Creation 4–5; packages/revud/src/direct/local-surface.ts createLocalReview; packages/app/src/components/create-local-review.test.ts 'names both refs when the histories are unrelated'

gaps.title: The D8 statement in the UI is untested
gaps.detail: §8.13 says the base-advance difference is 'worth stating in the UI'. pr-layout.tsx's base-advanced tooltip does state it, but the tooltip body renders through a portal and pr-layout.test.ts 'the base advanced' pins only the seal label, so the sentence can drift or vanish without a red test — and, per the major gap, it is never reachable on a local review anyway.

gaps.title: 'Re-sync to rebuild' is unfollowable for two corruption shapes (M8.8 OQ8, recorded, unowned)
gaps.detail: §8.15's graceful state is implemented via local-surface.ts rebuildable, which catches every StoreUnreadableError from the snapshot read and advises a re-sync. For a corrupt immutables row or a corrupt local_snapshots envelope the re-sync itself fails, so the remedy named cannot work. Recorded in tickets/M8.8-resync-and-pinning.md OQ8 and HANDOVER.md as belonging to whoever next owns store.ts; still open on this tree.

gaps.title: A failed pin is recorded but never surfaced
gaps.detail: §5.1/§8.12's mitigation degrades silently: performSync carries { pin: { ok: false, reason } } on LocalSyncOutcome (tested by local-surface.test.ts 'a failed pin is not a failed sync, and is reported'), but nothing renders or logs it (M8.8 OQ3, open), so a workspace whose update-ref fails loses the GC guarantee with no visible sign.

gaps.title: No real-git leg syncs a remote-tracking base to a successful snapshot; no mock fixture is dirty
gaps.detail: §8.3: the only real-git sync over a refs/remotes side is the same_ref failure leg (local-surface.test.ts 'a pair whose two sides sit on one commit is unprocessable'); listing and normalization are pinned but a successful origin/main-based snapshot is not. §8.16: the mock always writes dirty=false at sync (local.ts:544) and no seeded fixture sets dirty, so the banner is only proved by props-level tests (recorded in M8.7's Verify as a fixture gap).

gaps.title: Design schema text lags the store's unique key
gaps.detail: §8.6 and §4.2 state UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref); the store's key is UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation) with a constant generation = 0 (M8.2 ruling R-B, a no-migration escape hatch). Behaviour matches the promise; the design doc was not updated.

audits.label: Design §8 Edge cases — Writes, Archive, Retention, Security
audits.summary: Audited LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §8 Writes (17-19), Archive (20-22), Retention (23), Security (24-26) and §9 against the tree on board/m8.9-scratch-proof (tip of the #69..#84 stack; #84 OPEN, unmerged, check/conformance-matrix/e2e green). Every one of the ten concrete promises is implemented and pinned by a named test that reads the thing it claims: the shared supersedes() predicate has the fork row and the blank-never-matches rows; the seam is optional by the context's discriminated union and the detector is null without it, with a no-seam sync proven to issue zero requests under a throwing fetch double; archive is write-once on one column, freezes the sync, refuses all four verbs across matrix legs E/F/G, and a closed PR un-archives nothing; retention drops pinned refs and prunes unreferenced immutables after every successful local sync with the blob pass shipped dark under a recorded owner ruling; D7 is a source-scan allowlist including ./local-archive; the local port carries no appendAudit/putSnapshot, proved against a store that really has both; the synthesized author carries no address with a positive control. Case 18 (stale draft head on a conflict-terminated reconcile) was fixed in the app (setHead before submit) rather than inherited. §9 holds: nothing the code does contradicts its four exclusions and no later ticket delivered any of them. What does not hold is prose: the design's own "Zero eviction exists anywhere in the store today" and §3.1's MAX(id)+1 / three-column UNIQUE are now false against the store; the guide's "a local-only daemon that did resolve an origin ... archives exactly as any other does" omits the path-shaped-identity case that is never asked about; OQ10 (a draft PUT is accepted on a "read-only" archived review) is recorded but unruled; and no gate test reads the .mdx guides, so the drift class that once described a non-existent detector has no guard. No blockers, no majors.

items.text: Archiving is read-only, never destructive: threads, drafts and history stay visible, with a link to the PR, and the review freezes at the sync that found the PR. A PR closed without merging does not un-archive; creating the same pair again returns the archived review.

gaps.title: Guide overstates archive coverage for a workspace that gained its origin after the review was created
gaps.detail: packages/docs/content/docs/guides/local-review.mdx §7 says a local-only daemon that resolved an origin and a credential 'archives exactly as any other does'. A review created while the workspace had no origin stores an absolute-path repo identity (M8.9 OQ7, settled by M8.2), and the detector never asks about a path-shaped identity — packages/revud/src/direct/local-archive.ts isOwnerNameShaped, pinned by local-archive.test.ts 'a path-shaped repository identity is never asked about' — silently (requested:false, no warning). The ticket calls this intended; the guide does not say it.

gaps.title: 'Read-only' archived review still accepts draft writes — recorded as OQ10, unruled
gaps.detail: §8 #22 and the guide say an archived review is read-only; the conformance suite pins that a draft 'is still readable, and an edit still saves' on an archived review (packages/shared/conformance/local-archive.ts) and the scratch-repo proof found the inline gutter composer opens and PUT /api/pulls/<id>/draft answers 200. Recorded in M8.9 Open question 10 and BOARD.md as the owner's call, with neither answer taken; the write verbs that matter (submit/reply/resolve/reaction) do refuse. Not a broken promise — the design lists drafts under what stays available — but the word 'read-only' in the guide and design is broader than the behaviour the mock specifies.

gaps.title: No gate test reads the user-facing guides, so prose drift has no guard
gaps.detail: grep for '.mdx' across *.test.ts under packages/ and scripts/ finds nothing, and packages/docs carries no test files. The class of defect M8.11's adversarial pass caught ('a guide describing an archive detector that does not exist', BOARD.md) was fixed by hand and can recur unobserved. The present-tense claims in local-review.mdx, direct.mdx and security-review.md all match the code today (verified above), but only by this audit.

audits.label: Design §9 What this does not do
audits.summary: Audited docs/agent/LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §9 (four bullets: no cross-workspace review, no publishing to a PR ever, no review of uncommitted work, no shared database) against the tree at board/m8.9-scratch-proof, plus the user-facing guide, the run-modes pages and docs/security-review.md. All four §9 boundaries hold: the ownership guard answers not_found for a review another repository owns, the host collector never touches a local_* table, the local write sink has no GitHub client / decorator / runner and a source scan plus a fetch tripwire (leg G) and the e2e netlog pin it, the snapshot is built from a commit range with blobs read by SHA and the dirty flag is detected with `git status --porcelain=v1 -uno` and surfaced as the banner, and local rows live in the workspace's own SQLite under repo-scoped keys. Nothing the section defers was later delivered, so §9 is not stale, and nothing the code does contradicts it. What does not hold is minor: the guide (and inbox-sections.ts's own docstring) say the Local reviews section drops to the bottom "once they are all closed", but buildInboxSections places it first whenever any local row is listed, archived included, and the test named for the closed case passes zero local rows; the mock oracle never produces dirty:true so D3's warning is unspecified in the spec and undemonstrable under ?mock=1; no test asserts a worktree edit is absent from the synced diff (proved by construction only); LOCAL_REVIEWS.md §3.1/§4.2 still describe MAX(id)+1 minting and a three-column UNIQUE that the store replaced with a high-water mark and a generation column (recorded on the board); and M8.9 OQ10 (a draft PUT is accepted on an archived review) is recorded and awaiting the owner. No blocker and no major gap. PR #84 is OPEN on m8.12/delete-confirm with check, conformance-matrix and e2e passing.

gaps.title: Guide says the Local reviews section drops to the bottom once all are closed; code places it by row presence
gaps.detail: packages/docs/content/docs/guides/local-review.mdx §2 promises the section 'drops below every other section once they are all closed'. buildInboxSections in packages/app/src/lib/inbox-sections.ts returns `[localSection, ...pullRequestSections]` whenever `local.length > 0`, and `local` (from partitionInbox, id-only) includes archived rows because showsInInbox keeps a local review of any state — so a reader whose only local review is archived sees the section at the top. The module docstring repeats the doc's state-based wording. The test 'with none open but some held, the section sits below every other' (inbox-sections.test.ts) passes zero local rows, so it pins absence rather than closed state; 'is listed in exactly one section, and that section is the local one' seeds a closed local item and shows it lands in `local`. Fix is either the sentence (and docstring) or a state-aware placement plus a test that seeds `localItem(n, { state: 'closed' })` and asserts the bottom slot.

gaps.title: D3's exclusion half is proved by construction only — no test reads a synced snapshot after a worktree edit

votes.reasoning: The auditor's central factual claim is wrong and should be corrected: a test DOES drive a submit and a reply against a really deleted branch. packages/revud/src/direct/local-surface.test.ts, describe 'head resolution failures on ordinary repository states are typed', test 'a head branch deleted after the review was created answers a typed not-found naming the ref' (line 1327) builds a fixture repo, creates/syncs/submits/saves a draft, runs `git branch -q -D <head>`, then asserts submitReview and replyToThread each reject with ApiError code 'not_found' whose message contains `refs/heads/<head>`, and that the draft is byte-identical afterwards; it landed in fd2945c (2026-08-19) and I ran it green (2 pass, 9 expects). It is not vacuous: the sibling test at line 1395 proves the 'unprocessable' path is reachable, so removing the not_found throw in resolveLocalHead would turn the assertion red. The auditor's grep missed it because it asserts on the ref name, not the literal 'deleted or renamed'. However the gap as titled is still real in two ways. First, 'read-only' is only half-enforced at the daemon: only submitLocalReview (local-writes.ts:426) and replyToLocalThread (:680) call resolveHead; resolveLocalThread (:762) and addLocalReaction (:825) consult only the store, and the surface wrappers (local-surface.ts:1097-1113) add just requireReview, so on a vanished branch resolve and react succeed and mutate stored threads — contradicting the project's own definition of read-only (mock local.ts:872 'read-only means the stored content cannot change at all'; the archive path refuses all four verbs via writeOutcomes/refusedOutcomes in local-archive-sync.test.ts). Second, nothing in the app derives or renders read-only from a sync not_found: review-mode.ts reviewArchived/reviewComposerHidden gate only on mode==='local' && state==='closed'; pr-layout.tsx syncFailureCopy renders a toast 'Cached data is untouched.'; useSyncPull.onError (queries.ts:149) only reacts to 'network'; the composer stays live and the reviewer is refused only after typing and sending (review-bar.tsx:170 catch, thread-card.tsx submitReply onError). The mock (the spec, D6) cannot model a vanished ref at all — syncLocalReview (mock/local.ts:519) derives liveRefSha deterministically from the ref name — so no conformance leg pins it. The mechanism: createLocalReview's INSERT (packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts, ~line 1818) carries an explicit conflict target, `ON CONFLICT(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation) DO NOTHING`. SQLite validates an UPSERT's conflict target against the schema when the statement is prepared: if no UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY index exists over exactly that column set, the statement fails with "ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint". I verified this empirically in-memory under the tests' own runtime (bun 1.3.11, SQLite 3.51.0) using the identical INSERT text and identical column DDL: landed DDL with UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation) -> INSERT prepared and ran; UNIQUE clause deleted -> INSERT REFUSED; UNIQUE narrowed to (repo, base_ref, head_ref) with generation dropped -> INSERT REFUSED; same four columns in another order -> ran. That is measurably false. The mint in packages/revud/src/direct/store.ts `createLocalReview` inserts with `ON CONFLICT(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation) DO NOTHING`, and SQLite refuses to prepare an upsert whose conflict target does not exactly match a UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY on the table. I reproduced this with bun:sqlite in memory using the store's exact INSERT text: with `UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref, generation)` the insert lands (rows: 1); with the UNIQUE clause deleted it throws `ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint`; with the key narrowed to `UNIQUE(repo, base_ref, head_ref)` it throws the same. Because `db.run` is eager and the mint runs inside `write('local_reviews', …)`, the FIRST `createLocalReview` in every mint test would throw `StoreWriteError` — 'the same repo and branch pair mints once: a second create returns the first row', 'a superseded branch pair returns the superseded review, minting no successor', 'the same branch pair under two repositories are two distinct reviews', 'minted ids and their rows survive a close and reopen of the same data dir', and 'two live stores over one data dir mint one review for one branch pair' all go red. So the constraint — the full four-column key including `generation` — is implemented and behaviourally pinned: deleting it or dropping `generation` from it turns the suite red. The pin is not a comparison of two quantities that move together in the vacuous sense; the red condition is precisely "the UNIQUE key is absent or differently shaped from what the mint depends on". critic.overall: Every M8 milestone has code on the stack tip and a green gate behind it: creation, git-only sync, the four local writes, dispatch and boot relaxation, the inbox and chrome, re-sync with rewrite detection and pinning, archive-on-PR (proven live against revu-sandbox#6), retention, three-transport conformance, the e2e, the docs and the delete confirmation are all present and pinned somewhere non-vacuously. The four surviving majors are real but all sit on the edges of the flow — the missing real-mock parity leg, read-only after a vanished branch, no local walk of new-commit re-sync then reconcile, and staleness unreachable on a local review before a re-sync — and none breaks the loop a user runs day to day. What the audit missed is smaller in count but of the same kind the board itself warned about twice: an owner ruling with no implementing unit. Ruling 4 licensed unbounded pins only until retention arrived, and retention bounds immutables and (dark) blobs but never a live review's stale pins, so a rebased branch grows two refs per sync forever with nothing recording that as accepted. Two more user paths are unspecified by the mock and unpinned on any transport — deleting an archived review, and correcting a title the dialog itself mis-prefills — and the board's own ticket table has drifted (M8.10 at 4/7, units summing to 98). The honest status is: the feature has landed and the exit criteria hold on the tip, nothing has merged, and what remains before calling M8 closed is one afternoon of owner rulings (OQ10, ruling 4's pin bound, archived delete) plus the closers already listed, not more building.
